crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Sepsis Prediction
children.blurb: Sepsis prediction covers models that estimate whether a patient has sepsis or is likely to develop it, usually from electronic health record data such as vital signs, laboratory results, medication orders and nursing notes.

children.name: Acute Kidney Injury Prediction
children.blurb: Acute kidney injury prediction covers models that estimate whether a hospital patient's kidney function is about to decline, usually before creatinine rises far enough to meet the standard diagnostic criteria.

children.name: Ventilator Weaning
children.blurb: Ventilator weaning covers the clinical decision to reduce and then remove mechanical breathing support, and the predictive analytics built around that decision.

children.name: Fall Risk Monitoring
children.blurb: Fall risk monitoring covers systems that estimate how likely a patient is to fall and tools that alert staff when a fall may be happening.

children.name: Staffing and Bed Forecasting
children.blurb: Staffing and bed forecasting covers the models that predict how many nurses, doctors and beds a unit will need over the next shift, day or week.

sections.body: Predictive patient analytics in intensive care is the use of machine learning on clinical data to flag deterioration before it becomes obvious. In the ICU the signals are dense: vital signs, lab results, medication orders, ventilator settings and nursing notes, all timestamped. Models trained on this stream are used to raise sepsis alerts, estimate kidney injury risk, predict whether a patient can be taken off a ventilator, score fall risk on the ward, and forecast how many beds and nurses a unit will need. What is actually deployed is narrower than the research literature suggests, and most working systems sit inside the electronic record as a score or a flag rather than as an autonomous decision maker.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Sepsis prediction is the most studied and the most contested. Models can detect patterns hours before clinical recognition, but trials have shown that earlier alerts do not automatically translate into better outcomes, and alert fatigue is a real cost. Kidney injury prediction is more mature in its data foundations because creatinine and urine output are well structured, yet the gap between a risk score and a change in management remains. Ventilator weaning models perform reasonably at predicting extubation success, but the decision stays with the clinical team. Fall risk scoring is widely used and weakly predictive, and staffing and bed forecasting is largely an operations problem where the data is often messier than the clinical data. The honest limits are shared: shifting patient populations, missing values, site specific workflows, and the fact that a prediction is not an intervention.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the patient from admission to discharge and then step back to the unit as a whole. Sepsis Prediction and Acute Kidney Injury Prediction cover the two organ failures where early warning is most developed and most debated, and they are best read together because they share data sources and failure modes. Ventilator Weaning sits at the point where a prediction directly touches a daily decision about removing support. Fall Risk Monitoring moves out of the ICU to the general ward, where the data is sparser and the intervention is nursing care rather than a procedure. Staffing and Bed Forecasting closes the section by treating the unit itself as the patient, using the same forecasting logic on demand and capacity rather than on a single body.
